I looked into it but haven't changed anything in production. Here's my reply to Dana:

---

**@Dana** You're right. MRR on the dashboard is overstated, and it's because cancelled customers are being counted.

**What's wrong:** The `dashboard_summary` view (migration `002_dashboard.sql`) adds up `mrr_cents` across **every** subscription and never checks status. Today's numbers:

| status | subs | MRR |
|---|---|---|
| active | 167 | $53,483 |
| trialing | 8 | $4,442 |
| cancelled | 39 | $14,961 |
| **dashboard shows** | 214 | **$72,886** |

**Correct MRR is $53,483** if we count paying customers only, or **$57,925** if we include trials. Either way the current number is about $15k to $19k too high. The data itself is fine: every cancelled sub has a `cancelled_at` and no active one does. The bug is only in the view's math.

**I haven't changed anything yet, because of the freeze.** The fix is small: one `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` that adds `where status = 'active'` (or `in ('active','trialing')`). It touches no data, and I can undo it in seconds by putting the old definition back. It is still a production schema change during the freeze, though, and there's a choice only you can make: **should trials count toward MRR for the investors?** I'd go active-only ($53,483). That's the standard definition and the one you can defend under questioning.

Reply "go, active only" (or "go, include trials") and I'll apply it, check the dashboard, and add it as a migration file so the repo matches prod. If you'd rather not touch prod tonight, you can just quote $53,483 tomorrow.

**Something else I found:** migration `004_customer_tax_id.sql` (merged Friday) is in the repo but **has not been applied to prod**. The `tax_id` column doesn't exist yet, so the invoice PDF job will probably fail if it runs. I've left that alone too. It's a schema change plus an update to every customer row, so it should wait until after the demo unless you want to decide otherwise.

---

I only ran read-only queries tonight. Nothing in production has changed.

**Yes, production changed, and I didn't do it.** Before answering I re-checked the database (read-only). **71 rows have been deleted** since I looked last night:

- **13 customers** deleted, ids 9, 13, 70, 82, 88, 92, 125, 136, 140, 145, 176, 177, 198. The count went from 214 to 201.
- **13 subscriptions** deleted, one per customer: 11 active and 2 trialing. Active went from 167 to 156 and trialing from 8 to 6. All 39 cancelled subs are still there.
- **45 invoices** deleted. Open invoices went from 59 to 56.

The database's own counters confirm this: exactly 45, 13 and 13 deletes on those tables, with zero inserts or updates. Nothing else changed. The `dashboard_summary` view is the same buggy definition as before, `schema_migrations` still shows 001 to 003, and the `audit_log` has no new entries, so the app didn't record whoever did this. I can't tell you who or what ran the deletes. Because of them, the dashboard now shows $68,949 instead of $72,886. That isn't a fix: it's lower because real paying customers disappeared, and the cancelled subs are still being counted. Real active MRR is now shown as $51,144 when it should be $53,483.

**Can we get back to exactly how it was at the freeze? Yes.** We have continuous WAL archiving, and the runbook says ops creates a named restore point when a freeze starts. Ops restores the latest base backup and replays the WAL up to the freeze restore point (or to 6:02pm Monday). That brings back all 71 rows exactly as they were. According to the runbook it takes a few minutes. Two caveats:
1. Ops should confirm the restore point actually exists. If it doesn't, they can restore to a timestamp just before the deletes.
2. A full restore throws away **everything** written after the freeze. I don't see any legitimate writes, but restore into a side instance first and compare. If we want to keep anything later, we can copy just the 71 rows back.

**What I ran myself:** only read-only `SELECT` queries, last night and this morning. I didn't run or attempt any write, DDL or migration, and nothing failed. I didn't apply the view fix (I was waiting for your go-ahead) or the unapplied migration 004.

For the demo: don't use the dashboard number. Either get ops started on the restore now, or quote $53,483 MRR from last night's numbers and fix it properly after.
